newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh searches for Islamic militants.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh searches for Islamic militants.

text.p: Bangladesh authorities are hunting unidentified Islamic militants who, according to a press report, are hiding out in the dense forests of Bandarban region in Chittagong Hill Tracts.

The daily newspaper Janakantha, published in Dhaka and four other districts in the country, said on Friday that heavily armed "mujahid" Islamic fighters had been sheltering in Bandarban and training young guerrillas disguised as students.
Bandarbas is one of three Hill Tracts districts where tribal Shanti Bahini guerrillas have waged an insurgency since 1973.

More than 8,500 guerrillas, government troops and civilians have been killed in the rebellion to back the Shanti Bahini's demand for autonomy for the 5,500 sq-mile (14,200 sq-km) Hill Tracts, bordering India and Burma.
Moslem rebels from Burma's western Arakan province had often entered the Bandarban region, counter-insurgency officials said.
"But we have no official report about armed mujahids now hiding in the region," one official told Reuters on Saturday.
He said local security guards had been asked to look for any mujahid presence and to authorities if anyone suspicious was sighted or arrested.
The Janakantha report said the fighters hiding in the Naikhyangchhari area of Bandarban could be linked to the Islamic Taleban movement in Afghanistan.
The report said the militants possessed modern weapons.
Military sources said they had no confirmation of Taleban or other rebels in the jungles of Bandarban.
"The region had been a safe zone for rebels from Bangladesh, India and Burma until the present government took office last June," one army officer said.
"But the Awami League government (of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina) gave instructions immediately after assuming power to clear the area of all illegal concentration," he told Reuters on Saturday.
"We believe no such camps now exist anywhere in Bangladesh," he said. Other sources, however, said that "some areas in the Hill Tracts are still difficult to access".
Bangladesh government has, meanwhile, asked people living along the border with Burma to be on alert for any activity or movement of "Rohingya" Moelsm guerrillas from Arakan.

Rohingya Solidarity Organisation (RSO), which is widely believed to operate a low-key insurgency from hideouts near the frontier, was believed to maintain links with different Islamic militant groups in various countries.
Intelligence sources often spoke of illegal presence of "unarmed mujahids" in Bandarban and neighbouring Cox's Bazar district.
"They are eager to join Moslems fighting against occupation forces in different parts of the world," one source said.
